summary: When a man dies with no children, his brother usually does yibum or chalitzah with the widow. This mishnah lists fifteen close relatives of the brother who are free from this, and their co-wives are free too.

chunks.en: Fifteen women free their co-wives
chunks.st: Fifteen categories of women constitute familial relations that are forbidden as incestuous, and consequently, these women exempt their rival wives

words.note: A co-wife (tzarah) is another wife married to the same husband.

chunks.en: and the co-wives of their co-wives
chunks.st: and the rival wives of their rival wives

chunks.en: from chalitzah and from yibum
chunks.st: from ḥalitza and from levirate marriage

words.note: A ceremony that frees a widow from yibum.
When a man dies with no children, his brother marries the widow.

chunks.en: forever, all the way down the line.
chunks.st: forever, i.e., they also exempt rival wives of rival wives of rival wives, and so on.

chunks.en: And these are the women:
chunks.st: And these women are:

chunks.en: his daughter, and his daughter's daughter,
chunks.st: The daughter of the yavam, i.e., the deceased brother had married a daughter of his brother, which means that when he died childless, his brother’s own daughter came before her father for levirate marriage, and therefore she is exempt. And the same applies if the deceased brother’s widow is the daughter of the daughter of the yavam,

chunks.en: and his son's daughter,
chunks.st: or if she is the daughter of his son,

chunks.en: his wife's daughter,
chunks.st: or the daughter of his wife.

chunks.en: and his wife's son's daughter,
chunks.st: And similarly, if the yevama is the daughter of the son of the wife of her yavam

chunks.en: and his wife's daughter's daughter,
chunks.st: or the daughter of his wife’s daughter,

chunks.en: his mother-in-law, and his mother-in-law's mother,
chunks.st: or if she is the mother-in-law of her yavam, or his mother-in-law’s mother,

chunks.en: and his father-in-law's mother,
chunks.st: or his father-in-law’s mother, then she is exempt from ḥalitza and levirate marriage.

chunks.en: his sister from his mother,
chunks.st: The mishna continues its list of close relatives. If the yevama is the maternal half sister of the yavam,

chunks.en: and his mother's sister,
chunks.st: or if she is the sister of his mother, or

chunks.en: and his wife's sister,
chunks.st: his wife’s sister, then she is exempt from both ḥalitza and levirate marriage

chunks.en: and the wife of his brother from his mother,
chunks.st: Or if she was the wife of his maternal half brother, and after this brother died or divorced his wife, she married another of his father’s brothers, who was not her relative, and this brother died, she is exempt.
chunks.stMore: In this case, the obligation to enter into levirate marriage should be incurred by the surviving brother, but since she was previously the wife of his maternal brother, she is exempt.

chunks.en: and the wife of a brother who was not yet born when he lived,
chunks.explain: The second brother was born only after the first one died.
chunks.st: And the same applies to the wife of a brother with whom he did not coexist, i.e., the wife of a man who died before his brother was born.
chunks.stMore: As will be explained, the obligation of levirate marriage does not apply to the yavam in this case. Since levirate marriage does not apply to him, the yevama remains forbidden to him as his brother’s wife.

chunks.en: and his daughter-in-law.
chunks.st: And the last case is if one’s yevama had previously been his daughter-in-law, and after his son had died one’s brother married her, before he too passed away.

chunks.en: These free their co-wives
chunks.st: These fifteen women exempt their rival wives

chunks.en: and the co-wives of their co-wives
chunks.st: and the rival wives of their rival wives

chunks.en: from chalitzah and from yibum
chunks.st: from ḥalitza and levirate marriage

chunks.en: forever.
chunks.st: forever. §

chunks.en: But if any of them died,
chunks.explain: She died before her husband did.
chunks.st: And with regard to all of these women listed as prohibited relations, these halakhot apply only if they were married to the deceased brother until the time of his death. However, this is not the case if they died during the deceased brother’s lifetime,

chunks.en: or did mi'un,
chunks.st: or if they refused their husbands when they were minors.
chunks.stMore: This refusal is referring to the decree of the Sages that a girl under the age of twelve whose father is no longer alive may be married off by her mother or brothers. However, this marriage is not final, as she can terminate it by performing an act of refusal, i.e., by declaring, while still a minor, that she does not desire this marriage. In this case, the marriage is annulled retroactively and she is considered as though she were never married at all.

words.note: Mi'un: a young girl married off by her mother or brothers may say no to the marriage and end it.

chunks.en: or were divorced,
chunks.st: Or if those women were divorced by their husband, the deceased brother,

chunks.en: or turned out to be an aylonis,
chunks.st: or were found to be a sexually underdeveloped woman [aylonit], i.e., a woman who is so underdeveloped that she is not considered a woman in the full sense, these halakhot do not apply.
chunks.stMore: Her marriage is considered a mistaken marriage and is null and void.

words.note: A woman who cannot have children; her marriage was a mistake.

chunks.en: then their co-wives are allowed.
chunks.st: In all these cases their rival wives are permitted, as the exemption for rival wives of forbidden relatives applies only when the forbidden relative was the brother’s wife at the time of his death, when the halakhot of levirate marriage came into effect. §

chunks.en: And you cannot say
chunks.st: And the mishna comments that the language of this principle is imprecise, as you cannot say with regard to

chunks.en: about his mother-in-law, her mother, or his father-in-law's mother
chunks.st: his mother-in-law and with regard to his mother-in-law’s mother and with regard to his father-in-law’s mother

chunks.en: that they turned out to be an aylonis,
chunks.explain: She has children, so she cannot be an aylonis.
chunks.st: that they were found to be an aylonit, as an aylonit is sterile and therefore cannot become a mother or a mother-in-law.

chunks.en: or that they did mi'un.
chunks.explain: Mi'un is only for young girls, who could not be a mother.
chunks.st: Nor is the mishna precise when it states: Or refused, as refusal applies only to minors, who cannot give birth.

summary: This mishnah shows how a forbidden relative frees her co-wife, and even the co-wife's co-wife. But if the relative died or was divorced first, her co-wife is not freed.

chunks.en: How do they free their co-wives?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: How do these women exempt their rival wives?

chunks.en: If his daughter, or any one of
chunks.st: If, for example, his daughter or any one of

chunks.en: these forbidden relatives, was married to his brother,
chunks.st: those women with whom relations are forbidden was married to his brother

words.note: Women a man may not marry because they are close family.

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: and this brother had another wife,

chunks.en: and he died, just as his daughter is free,
chunks.st: and the brother died, then just as his daughter is exempt from levirate marriage,

chunks.en: so her co-wife is free.
chunks.st: so too her rival wife is exempt. If

chunks.he: הָלְכָה צָרַת בִּתּוֹ וְנִשֵּׂאת לְאָחִיו הַשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: If his daughter's co-wife went and married his second brother,
chunks.st: his daughter’s rival wife subsequently went and married his second brother, to whom she is permitted,

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: and he had another wife,

chunks.en: and he died, just as his daughter's co-wife is free,
chunks.st: and he died childless as well, which means that his wife comes before the first yavam, the daughter’s father, for levirate marriage, then just as his daughter’s rival wife is exempt,

chunks.en: so her co-wife's co-wife is free,
chunks.st: so too the rival wife of her rival wife is exempt. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: even if there are a hundred of them.
chunks.st: Even if they are one hundred brothers, the same logic applies.
chunks.stMore: If a woman is exempt from levirate marriage because she is the rival wife of a forbidden relative or the rival wife of a rival wife of this kind, and she herself has an additional rival wife, this rival wife is also exempt and in turn exempts her own rival wives from levirate marriage.

chunks.en: How is it that if they died, their co-wives are allowed?
chunks.st: How so? What are the cases in which if they died their rival wives are permitted?

chunks.en: If his daughter, or any one of
chunks.st: If, for example, one’s daughter or any one of

chunks.en: these forbidden relatives, was married to his brother,
chunks.st: those women with whom relations are forbidden was married to his brother, and this brother

chunks.en: and he had another wife,
chunks.st: had another wife,

chunks.en: and his daughter died or was divorced,
chunks.st: and then his daughter died or was divorced

chunks.en: and after that his brother died,
chunks.st: and afterward his brother died,

chunks.en: her co-wife is allowed.
chunks.st: her rival wife is permitted to him. §

chunks.en: And any girl who could do mi'un but did not,
chunks.explain: Her marriage was only from the Rabbis, not fully from the Torah.
chunks.st: The mishna states another principle: And if any of these forbidden relatives was a minor who could refuse her husband, then even if she did not refuse,

chunks.en: her co-wife does chalitzah, but not yibum.
chunks.st: her rival wife performs ḥalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: The rival wife may not enter into levirate marriage, as she is the rival wife of a forbidden relative. However, she is not entirely exempt from levirate marriage and must be released by ḥalitza because the marriage of the forbidden relative was not a fully valid marriage, and therefore, by Torah law, the other woman is not considered a rival wife of a forbidden relative.

summary: Six relatives are forbidden even more strictly, because they can never marry any of the brothers. So yibum does not apply at all, and their co-wives are allowed.

chunks.en: Six forbidden relatives are stricter than these,
chunks.st: Six women with whom relations are forbidden who were not enumerated in the first mishna are forbidden by prohibitions that are more severe than those listed in that mishna

chunks.en: because they are married to others,
chunks.explain: They are never married to a brother, so yibum never applies.
chunks.st: because they may be married only to others and may never be married to any of the brothers, due to the closeness of their relationship.
chunks.stMore: However, this stringency entails a corresponding leniency: Since the halakha of levirate marriage is entirely inapplicable in these cases,

chunks.en: so their co-wives are allowed.
chunks.st: their rival wives are permitted.
chunks.stMore: The rival wife of a forbidden relative is forbidden herself only if the mitzva of levirate marriage is applicable, but where it is not in effect she is permitted. The six women with whom relations are forbidden are as follows:

chunks.en: His mother, and his father's wife,
chunks.st: His mother, and his father’s wife,

chunks.en: and his father's sister,
chunks.st: and his father’s sister,

chunks.en: his sister from his father,
chunks.st: and his paternal half sister,

chunks.en: and the wife of his father's brother,
chunks.st: and the wife of his father’s brother,

chunks.en: and the wife of his brother from his father.
chunks.st: and the wife of his paternal half brother.
chunks.stMore: Each of these women with whom relations are forbidden is forbidden equally to all of the brothers, and the mitzva of levirate marriage is inapplicable. Therefore, her rival wife is permitted.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue whether these co-wives may marry the brothers. Even so, the two groups still married into each other's families and trusted each other's purity.
stIntro: Up to this point, the discussions were based on the assumption that not only may a forbidden relative not enter into levirate marriage, but her rival wife is also exempt. However, this issue is subject to a long-standing dispute.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai allow the co-wives to the brothers,
chunks.explain: Beis Shammai say the co-wife of a forbidden relative may do yibum.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai permit the rival wives to the brothers, as they did not accept the interpretation of the verses that indicates that rival wives are prohibited.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel forbid them.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel forbid them. The previous mishnayot are in accordance with the opinion of Beit Hillel.

chunks.he: חָלְצוּ, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין מִן הַכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: If they did chalitzah, Beis Shammai make them unfit to marry a Kohen,
chunks.explain: A woman who did chalitzah may not marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: If any of the rival wives of the brother performed ḥalitza, Beit Shammai disqualify her from marrying into the priesthood, as in their opinion these rival wives were fit for levirate marriage, which means that the ḥalitza was fully valid.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, they are disqualified from marrying a priest, like all other women who perform ḥalitza.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say they are fit.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel deem them fit, as they maintain that no legal act of ḥalitza was performed here at all.

chunks.en: If they did yibum, Beis Shammai say they are fit,
chunks.st: If they entered into levirate marriage, Beit Shammai deem them fit for the priesthood, as in their opinion, this is a fully legal levirate marriage.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel make them unfit.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel disqualify them, because they engaged in licentious sexual relations as the rival wives of a forbidden relative.

chunks.en: Even though these
chunks.st: § The mishna comments: Although Beit Hillel

chunks.en: forbid and these allow,
chunks.st: prohibit the rival wives to the brothers and Beit Shammai permit them, and although

chunks.en: these make unfit and these say fit,
chunks.st: these disqualify these women and those deem them fit,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai did not stop
chunks.st: Beit Shammai did not refrain

chunks.en: marrying women from Beis Hillel,
chunks.st: from marrying women from Beit Hillel,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel did not stop marrying women from Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: nor did Beit Hillel refrain from marrying women from Beit Shammai.

chunks.en: And in all the questions of tahor and tamei,
chunks.st: Furthermore, with regard to all of the disputes concerning the halakhot of ritual purity and impurity, where these rule that an article is

chunks.en: where these said tahor and these said tamei,
chunks.st: ritually pure and those rule it ritually impure,

chunks.en: they did not stop handling pure things
chunks.st: they did not refrain from handling ritually pure objects

chunks.en: with each other.
chunks.explain: They trusted each other's dishes and food.
chunks.st: each with the other, as Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel frequently used each other’s vessels.
